newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up on pre-report positioning.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up on pre-report positioning.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended with modest gains on Monday as traders took positions before the next supply and demand report from the U.S. Deapartment of Agriculture on Wednesday, traders said.
"We are just waiting for the report," said one floor trader. "There's been no trade all day."

Some analysts and traders are looking for USDA to shave the already small 1996-97 soybean carryout. In its January report, USDA estimated soybean ending stocks at 155 million bushels. That estimate was down sharply from their previous one of 180 million.

Many also expect the USDA to raise crop production forecasts for both the Brazilian and Argentine soybean crops. In its last report, USDA put the Brazilian crop at 25.90 million tonnes and the Argentine crop at 12.65 million.
Some bullish traders described USDA's weekly export inspections of 19.86 million as disappointing.
"The wheat and (soy)bean inspections were certainly nothing to write home about," said Victor Lespinasse, floor broker with Dean Witter in Chicago.
CBOT soybeans closed up two to five cents per bushel with March up two at $7.40 and May up two at $7.38-1/2.
There was also talk on the trading floor that a U.S. commercial firm had a vessel on the way to Brazil to pick up new crop soybeans for shipment to European crushers, trade sources said.

In late trading, Merrill Lynch and Prudential Securities were noted buyers. On the day, L.B. Stern bought 500,000 bushels March and Cargill sold one million bushels March. ING sold 600,000 bushels March.
The Chicago Board of Trade estimated Monday's soybean volume at 40,000 contracts. That figure was slightly lower than Friday's final volume of 43,176 contracts.
In options trading, Tenco bought 100 March $7.50 calls and ING bought 100 November $7.75 calls, floor sources said.
